overthinker.name: Overthinker
overthinker.tagline: Racing thoughts, endless replays, analysis paralysis
overthinker.description: Your anxiety lives inside your head. While others feel stress in their body or social situations, your mind becomes a runaway train of thoughts, replays, and what-ifs. You analyze conversations from three weeks ago, rewrite emails in your head at 2 AM, and create elaborate mental scenarios for events that may never happen. Your brain is always running, always processing, always searching for the thing you missed. The gift is your depth of thought; the burden is that the off-switch doesn't work.
overthinker.trait3: Mind won't quiet down at night

perfectionist.name: Perfectionist
perfectionist.tagline: Nothing is ever good enough, including yourself
perfectionist.description: Your anxiety is fueled by impossibly high standards that you hold yourself to — and sometimes others. Every task must be done flawlessly, every detail must be right, and anything less than perfection feels like failure. You revise, redo, and overwork not because you want to, but because the anxiety of 'not good enough' is unbearable. Procrastination isn't laziness — it's fear of starting something you can't do perfectly. Your strength is your excellence; your prison is that you can never meet your own expectations.

socialWorrier.name: Social Worrier
socialWorrier.tagline: Everyone is watching, everyone is judging
socialWorrier.description: For you, other people are both the source and audience of your anxiety. You walk into a room and immediately scan for signs of judgment. You replay social interactions wondering what you said wrong, convince yourself people are upset with you on no evidence, and avoid situations where you might be the center of attention. Your anxiety tells you that you're being evaluated every second, and you're always one misstep away from social exile. Your empathy runs deep; so does your self-consciousness.

bodyAlarm.name: Body Alarm
bodyAlarm.tagline: Your body sounds the alarm before your mind even catches up
bodyAlarm.description: While others think their way into anxiety, your body gets there first. Racing heart, tight chest, nauseous stomach, dizzy head, trembling hands — your nervous system fires the alarm before your brain even registers the threat. You might not always know why you feel anxious, but your body always knows. Physical symptoms can spiral into panic attacks, health anxiety, or a constant state of tension that exhausts you. Your body is hyper-vigilant; learning to trust it is your journey.
bodyAlarm.trait3: Body stays tense even when calm

futureDreader.name: Future Dreader
futureDreader.tagline: What if everything goes wrong? It probably will.
futureDreader.description: Your anxiety isn't about the present — it's about what hasn't happened yet. You live in a future that is always threatening, always uncertain, always about to go wrong. You catastrophize, imagining worst-case scenarios in vivid detail. A cough becomes cancer. A meeting becomes termination. A plane ticket becomes a crash. Your mind is a prediction machine set permanently to 'worst outcome.' The irony is that the present moment is usually fine — but you're rarely there to enjoy it.
futureDreader.trait2: Lives in the future, not the present

controlSeeker.name: Control Seeker
controlSeeker.tagline: If I can't control it, I can't handle it
controlSeeker.description: Your anxiety spikes whenever things feel uncertain or out of your hands. You need plans, structure, backup plans, and backup plans for your backup plans. Spontaneity feels threatening. Delegating feels dangerous. If you can't predict it, prepare for it, or manage it, the anxiety floods in. You create elaborate systems, checklists, and routines — not because you love organization, but because chaos is terrifying. Your reliability is your superpower; your rigidity is your cage.
